blocks.title: You'll want to know: ですか

segments.text: ですか — desu ka — "is it...?". です, desu, says politely that something is so. Put か, ka, at the end, and the sentence becomes a question that can be answered yes or no. The order of the words does not change, and the voice rises a little on ka.
これは みずですか。 — kore wa mizu desu ka — "Is this water?" はい、みずです。 — hai, mizu desu — "Yes, it is water."
A verb takes か the same way: ます becomes ますか.
あした はたらきますか。 — ashita hatarakimasu ka — "Are you working tomorrow?"

blocks.title: You'll want to know: ちがいます

segments.text: ちがいます — chigaimasu — "it is different", and so, as an answer, "no, that is not right". It is the polite form of the verb ちがう, chigau, "to differ". When someone asks whether a thing is so and it is not, this is the everyday answer.
これは おちゃですか。 — kore wa ocha desu ka — "Is this tea?" いいえ、ちがいます。みずです。 — iie, chigaimasu. mizu desu — "No, it isn't. It is water."

blocks.title: You'll want to know: じゃない

segments.text: じゃない — ja nai — "is not". It is the plain way, among friends, to say that something is not so. The polite way is じゃありません, ja arimasen.
みずじゃない。 — mizu ja nai — "It isn't water."
Verbs say not with their ending. In the polite form, ます becomes ません, masen:
はたらきます becomes はたらきません — hatarakimasen — "I don't work" ねます becomes ねません — nemasen — "I don't go to bed".

blocks.title: You'll want to know: なにも

segments.text: なにも — nani mo — "nothing", "not anything". It pairs with a negative verb: Japanese says "anything... not", where English says "nothing".
なにも のみません。 — nani mo nomimasen — "I don't drink anything."
のむ, nomu, "to drink", gives のみます nomimasu and then のみません nomimasen. With ます instead of ません the sentence does not work: なにも (nani mo) needs the not.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: だれも

segments.text: だれも — dare mo — "nobody", "not anyone". Like なにも (nani mo), it needs a negative verb.
ここには だれも いません。 — koko ni wa dare mo imasen — "There is nobody here."
いません, imasen, is the negative of います, imasu, "someone is there", the verb Japanese uses for people and animals.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: どこにも

segments.text: どこにも — doko ni mo — "nowhere", "not anywhere". It is どこ, "where", with に for the place you go to and も, and like the other two it needs a negative verb.
あしたは どこにも いきません。 — ashita wa doko ni mo ikimasen — "I'm not going anywhere tomorrow."
Now you can ask and answer:
あした はたらきますか。 — "Are you working tomorrow?" いいえ、はたらきません。どこにも (doko ni mo) いきません。 — "No, I'm not. I'm not going anywhere."
